_comment: Curated source manifest for Compendium. This is the curation decision itself —
'the value is in what you left out' — so it lives in git. Corpus *text* does not.
Every entry is permitted under the corpus rules in README.md. Nothing from GDC
Vault, published books, or paid postmortems. Entries that are denied by policy
are kept rather than deleted, so the rule is visible on every ingest instead of
Deliberately flat and denormalised. This is data, not schema.
Run corpus/verify_sources.py before trusting any URL in this file.

sources.title: Water Rendering in Far Cry 5
sources.note: In this 2018 GDC session, AMD's Cristian Cutocheras and Ubisoft's Branislav Grujic discuss the Far Cry team's all-new water system that applies to a number of new water materials that allow the artists to create realistic water-based physical features such as waterfalls and lakes

sources.title: From Shore to Horizon: Creating a Practical Tessellation Based Solution
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC talk, Eidos Montreal's Jean-Normand Bucci and Nicolas Longchamps discuss the techniques behind their Ocean Technology system.

sources.title: The Latest Graphics Technology in Remedy's Northlight Engine
sources.note: In this 2018 GDC talk, Remedy's Taatu Aalto discusses the in-engine implementation and results of some recent advances in rendering technology in Remedy's Northlight engine.

sources.title: High Dynamic Range Color Grading and Display in Frostbite
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC talk, EA's Alex Fry presents the approach the Frostbite team took to add support for HDR displays.

sources.title: Geometry Caching Optimizations in Halo 5: Guardians
sources.note: Geometry Caching Optimizations in Halo 5: Guardians

sources.title: The Illusion of Motion: Making Magic with Textures in the Vertex Shader
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC session, Tequila Works' Mario Palmero presents ways to use textures in vertex shaders as a cheaper alternative solution to established methods, and present a new technique for animation pipelines that bypasses the CPU and enables animators to increase bone counts dramatically.

sources.title: Global Illumination in Tom Clancy's The Division
sources.note: In this 2016 GDC talk, Ubisoft's Nikolay Stefanov describes the dynamic global illumination system that Ubisoft Massive created for Tom Clancy's The Division.

sources.title: Rendering Rainbow Six Siege
sources.note: In this 2016 GDC session, Ubisoft Montreal's Jalal Eddine El Mansouri describes the most interesting work done by the R6 graphics team to ship Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege on Xbox One, PS4 and up to 5 year old PCs, while focusing on architectural optimizations that leverages compute that are only possible with the current generation hardware

sources.title: Low Complexity, High Fidelity: The Rendering of INSIDE
sources.note: In this 2016 GDC Europe session, PlayDead's  Mikkel Gjoel and Mikkel Svendsen detail the techniques used to achieve high visual fidelity in the context of the uncompromisingly simplistic aesthetic of INSIDE, Playdead's follow-up to the critically acclaimed LIMBO.

sources.title: AI Arborist: Proper Cultivation and Care for Your Behavior Trees
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC talk, Bobby Anguelov, Mika Vehkala, and Ben Weber outline core principles to get the most out of your behavior trees while avoiding common issues.

sources.title: Tree's Company: Systemic AI Design in Just Cause 3
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC session, Avalanche Studios'  Robert Meyer details exactly what technical designs, interfaces, and methods Avalanche used to keep its AI systemic and robust, yet flexible and controllable enough for content creators.

sources.title: Hacking into the Combat AI of Watch Dogs 2
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC talk, Ubisoft's Chae Dickie-Clark shows how the NPCs of Watch Dogs 2 efficiently process their environment to select cover and perform other dynamic behaviors thanks to an intricate AI system designed by the Ubisoft team.

sources.title: Taking Back What's Ours: The AI of Dishonored 2
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC session, Arkane Studios' Laurent Couvidou and Xavier Sadoulet explain how the AI of Dishonored 2 was designed for a variety of systems including coordination of multiple NPCs, spatial reasoning for stealth and search, and a data-driven rule system for dialog and animations.

sources.title: AI & Animation in Assassin's Creed Brotherhood
sources.note: In this 2011 GDC session, Ubisoft's Nicolas Barbeau and Aleissia Laidacker discuss the AI and animation powering the virtual population of Rome in Assassin's Creed Brotherhood.

sources.title: Nuts and Bolts: Modular AI From the Ground Up
sources.note: In this 2016 GDC panel, programmers Kevin Dill, Christopher Dragert & Troy Humphreys provide a comprehensive exploration of modular AI, from the theoretical underpinnings up to code examples from shipped titles.

sources.title: Modeling AI Perception and Awareness in Splinter Cell: Blacklist
sources.note: In this 2014 GDC talk, Ubisoft Toronto's Martin Walsh describes the AI stealth models used on Splinter Cell: Blacklist, the reason for using them, issues that came up, and Ubisoft's overall strategy for giving consistent feedback to the player while maintaining realism.

sources.title: Creating Complex AI Behavior in Stellaris Through Data-Driven Design
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC talk, Paradox Interactive's Mehrnaz Amanat Bari covers the design and implementation of data driven AI in Stellaris to create NPCs with unique and non static personalities in a decision based game.

sources.title: Goal-Oriented Action Planning: Ten Years of AI Programming
sources.note: In this 2015 GDC talk, AI Programmers Chris Conway, Peter Higley and Eric Jacopin revisit the Goal-Oriented Action Planning method of game AI programming to see how it's held up for the last 10 years, and how it influenced the AI of Middle Earth: Shadow of Mordor and Tomb Raider.

sources.title: Mind Your Step: Avoiding 3 Common Pitfalls in AI Development
sources.note: In this 2016 GDC session, Insomniac Games' Jan Mueller challenges 3 common misconceptions about best practices in AI design.

sources.title: Tom Clancy's The Division: AI Behavior Editing and Debugging
sources.note: Tom Clancy's The Division features a large number of NPCs with a wide range of complex behaviors. The designers needed to be able to manage the creation, editing and debugging of the NPC AI in an effective, understandable and efficient way. This 2016 lecture from Massive Entertainment's Jonas Gillberg showa how this is made possible using the technology of the Snowdrop engine. This talk includes an introduction to how behavior trees are structured and how their logic works.

sources.title: Can You See Me Now? Building Robust AI Sensory Systems
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC talk, Ubisoft's Eric Martel describes how to construct advanced sensory systems to allow AI to better respond to player inputs.

sources.title: Virtual Insanity: Meta AI on Assassin's Creed: Origins
sources.note: In this 2018 GDC session, Ubisoft's Charles Lefebvre discusses the creation of Meta AI for Assassin's Creed: Origins and how its objects could be virtual or real, in formations, in conflict, be part of a mission or autonomous, and how they can have a persistent inventory.

sources.title: Knowledge is Power: An Overview of Knowledge Representation in Game AI
sources.note: In this 2018 GDC talk, Daniel Brewer and Rez Graham explain best practices for helping video game AI make decisions that will feel impactful to the player.

sources.title: Physics for Game Programmers: Understanding Constraints
sources.note: This session will be about writing a character controller. Erin will show how to implement a character controller using swept collision and an iterative solver. The solver naturally handles collision priorities using Lagrange multipliers.

sources.title: Supercharged! Vehicle Physics in Skylanders
sources.note: In this 2016 GDC talk, Vicarious Visions' Jan Erik Steel & Patrick Donnelly  cover how land, sea and air physics handling for Skylanders Superchargers was created, exploring how they managed the complexities of the physical simulation while always striving for a simple and intuitive designer interface and tools.

sources.title: Physics for Game Programmers; Continuous Collision
sources.note: In this 2013 GDC session, Blizzard Entertainment's Erin Catto explores how to solve collision problems in game programming.

sources.title: It IS Rocket Science! The Physics of Rocket League Detailed
sources.note: In this 2018 GDC talk, Psyonix's Jared Cone takes viewers through an inside look at the specific game design decisions and implementation details that made the networked physics of Rocket League so successful.

sources.title: Math for Game Programmers: Juicing Your Cameras With Math
Math for Game Programmers: Predictable Projectiles
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC talk, Robot Entertainment's Chris Stark explains the math and code behind predictive linear and ballistic projectile aiming, how to handle practical variations, and best practices for exposing knobs to designers.

sources.title: Animation Bootcamp: An Indie Approach to Procedural Animation
sources.note: In this 2014 GDC session, indie developer David Rosen explains how to use simple procedural techniques to achieve interactive and fluid animations using very few key frames, with examples from indie games like Overgrowth, Receiver and Black Shades.

sources.title: Stress-Free Game Development: Powering Up Your Studio With DevOps
sources.note: In this 2020 GDC Virtual Talk, Butterscotch Shenanigans' Seth Coster walks through how his team learned to use DevOps to get more done while working less.

sources.title: Overwatch Gameplay Architecture and Netcode
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC session, Blizzard's Timothy Ford explains how Overwatch uses the Entity Component System (ECS) architecture to create a rich variety of layered gameplay.

sources.title: I Shot You First: Networking the Gameplay of Halo: Reach
sources.note: In this 2011 GDC session, Bungie's David Aldridge discusses the programming that drove Halo: Reach's online networking.

sources.title: Replicating Chaos: Vehicle Replication in Watch Dogs 2
sources.note: In this 2017 GDC session, Ubisoft Toronto's Matt Delbosc explores the techniques used in Watch Dogs 2 to replicate vehicle trajectories, compensate for network latency, and realistically represent vehicle-versus-vehicle collisions between players.
